title: Closed-ideal quotients of complete normed commutative rings
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative unital ring with a norm $N:R\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ such that $N(x)=0$ exactly for $x=0$, $N(-x)=N(x)$, $N(x+y)\le N(x)+N(y)$ and $N(xy)\le N(x)N(y)$. Suppose $R$ is complete for the metric $N(x-y)$, and let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal closed for this metric topology. On the quotient ring $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] put $\overline N(\overline x)=\inf_{y\in I}N(x+y)$. Then $\overline N$ is a norm with the same ring inequalities, $R/I$ is complete for it, and its norm topology is the quotient topology. The projection $\pi:R\to R/I$ is continuous and open and satisfies $\overline N(\pi(x))\le N(x)$. The ideal $I=R$ and the zero quotient ring are allowed.

from.place: Historical analytic input supporting the normalization chain from lem-trf-local-term-locality, through Temkin Theorem 3.5.5 Step 2: Distinguished presentations of reduced affinoids over an algebraically closed field. This is below the node level, not a replacement of the current contracting-correspondence unit proof. Supporting analytic lemma in the presentation construction: Norm-preserving lifts for a Tate epimorphism surjective on canonical reductions. Independent analytic input: Finite affinoid maps are finite on spectral unit balls over an algebraically closed field. Proof input: Minimal components give an isometric affinoid embedding. General topological input for the component-quotient clause: completeness and quotient topology after dividing the Tate algebra by the inverse image of a minimal prime.
